proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Ozone gas is introduced into the liquid stream via a T-junction to create a segmented or dispersed flow regime, maximizing gas-liquid interfacial area for mass transfer. Quench is added downstream after complete ozonolysis to prevent accumulation of unstable ozonides.
pre_reactor_steps: Cool Stream A (Alkene) to -20 C using a pre-cooler coil.
Generate Ozone/O2 mixture (approx 5-10% O3 in O2) using an ozone generator.
Mix Stream A and Stream B at T-junction 1.
post_reactor_steps: Pass ozonide solution through a back-pressure regulator (BPR) to maintain pressure.
Mix with Stream C (DMS Quench) at T-junction 2.
Allow short residence time (1-2 min) in a second coiled tube for quenching.
Vent excess gas through an ozone destroyer (catalytic or thermal) before atmospheric release.
proposal.chemistry_notes: Ozonolysis is highly exothermic. The low temperature (-20 C) and small reactor volume (5 mL) minimize thermal runaway risk. DMS is used to reduce the primary ozonide (molozonide) and secondary ozonide to carbonyl compounds. The stoichiometry assumes 1 eq alkene reacts with 1 eq O3 to form ozonide, which requires 2 eq DMS for complete reduction. Excess O3 is vented safely.

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: 5 minutes is sufficient for complete ozonolysis of simple alkenes at -20 C with good gas-liquid contact.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: 1 mL/min is a standard low-flow rate for hazardous reactions to minimize inventory.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: -20 C is specified in the batch protocol to control exotherm and stability.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.05 M matches the batch protocol to ensure comparable kinetics and safety margins.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 10 bar ensures the solvent (DCM, bp 40 C) remains liquid at -20 C and prevents gas bubble expansion, maintaining consistent residence time.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Coiled PTFE tubing is chemically resistant to ozone and DCM, and allows for efficient heat exchange.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID provides a high surface-area-to-volume ratio for gas-liquid mass transfer.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: Calculated as (Flow Rate * Residence Time) = 1 mL/min * 5 min = 5 mL. This small volume minimizes the inventory of explosive ozonides.
reasoning_per_field.streams: Stream A is the substrate. Stream B is the oxidant. Stream C is the reductive workup. Gas flow is adjusted to provide slight excess O3.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-junctions are simple and effective for initial gas-liquid mixing and subsequent liquid-liquid quenching.
safety_flags: Ozone is toxic and corrosive; ensure proper ventilation and destruction.
Ozonides are potentially explosive; keep inventory low and avoid evaporation to dryness.
DMS has a strong odor; use closed system.
DCM is toxic; use appropriate PPE.

proposal.literature_analogies: Continuous flow ozonolysis has been demonstrated by various groups (e.g., Jensen, Noël) using similar PTFE coils and low temperatures to safely handle ozonides.
